answer_text:
Let

\[
x^1=x,\qquad x^2=y,
\]

and

\[
g_{11}=g_{22}=\frac1{y^2},\qquad g_{12}=0.
\]

Thus

\[
g^{11}=g^{22}=y^2,\qquad g^{12}=0.
\]

## 1. Christoffel symbols

The Christoffel symbols are

\[
\Gamma^k_{ij}
=
\frac12 g^{k\ell}
\left(
\frac{\partial g_{j\ell}}{\partial x^i}
+
\frac{\partial g_{i\ell}}{\partial x^j}
-
\frac{\partial g_{ij}}{\partial x^\ell}
\right).
\]

Since the metric depends only on \(y=x^2\), the only nonzero first derivatives are

\[
\frac{\partial g_{11}}{\partial y}
=
\frac{\partial g_{22}}{\partial y}
=
-\frac{2}{y^3}.
\]

Hence the nonzero Christoffel symbols are

\[
\Gamma^1_{12}=\Gamma^1_{21}
=
\frac12 y^2\left(-\frac{2}{y^3}\right)
=
-\frac1y,
\]

\[
\Gamma^2_{11}
=
\frac12 y^2\left(-\frac{\partial g_{11}}{\partial y}\right)
=
\frac1y,
\]

\[
\Gamma^2_{22}
=
\frac12 y^2\frac{\partial g_{22}}{\partial y}
=
-\frac1y.
\]

All other Christoffel symbols vanish.

## 2. Compute \(R_{1212}\)

Using the given formula

\[
R_{klij}
=
\frac12
\left(
\frac{\partial^2 g_{il}}{\partial x^j\partial x^k}
+
\frac{\partial^2 g_{jk}}{\partial x^i\partial x^\ell}
-
\frac{\partial^2 g_{ik}}{\partial x^j\partial x^\ell}
-
\frac{\partial^2 g_{jl}}{\partial x^i\partial x^\ell}
+
g_{rs}\Gamma^r_{jk}\Gamma^s_{il}
-
g_{rs}\Gamma^r_{jl}\Gamma^s_{ik}
\right),
\]

take

\[
k=1,\qquad \ell=2,\qquad i=1,\qquad j=2.
\]

So we want \(R_{1212}\).

The only nonzero second derivative appearing is

\[
\frac{\partial^2 g_{11}}{\partial y^2}
=
\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(-\frac{2}{y^3}\right)
=
\frac{6}{y^4}.
\]

All terms involving \(\partial/\partial x\) vanish. Therefore the derivative part gives

\[
\frac12\left(
-\frac{\partial^2 g_{11}}{\partial y^2}
\right)
=
-\frac12\cdot \frac{6}{y^4}
=
-\frac{3}{y^4}.
\]

Now compute the Christoffel-symbol part:

\[
g_{rs}\Gamma^r_{21}\Gamma^s_{12}
-
g_{rs}\Gamma^r_{22}\Gamma^s_{11}.
\]

The only nonzero contribution in the first term is \(r=s=1\):

\[
g_{11}\Gamma^1_{21}\Gamma^1_{12}
=
\frac1{y^2}\left(-\frac1y\right)\left(-\frac1y\right)
=
\frac1{y^4}.
\]

The only nonzero contribution in the second term is \(r=s=2\):

\[
g_{22}\Gamma^2_{22}\Gamma^2_{11}
=
\frac1{y^2}\left(-\frac1y\right)\left(\frac1y\right)
=
-\frac1{y^4}.
\]

Thus the Christoffel-symbol part is

\[
\frac1{y^4}-\left(-\frac1{y^4}\right)
=
\frac{2}{y^4}.
\]

Therefore

\[
R_{1212}
=
-\frac{3}{y^4}+\frac{2}{y^4}
=
-\frac{1}{y^4}.
\]

## 3. Compute the curvature \(K\)

The denominator is

\[
g_{11}g_{22}-g_{12}^2
=
\frac1{y^2}\cdot \frac1{y^2}-0
=
\frac1{y^4}.
\]

Hence

\[
K
=
\frac{R_{1212}}{g_{11}g_{22}-g_{12}^2}
=
\frac{-1/y^4}{1/y^4}
=
-1.
\]

Thus the curvature is constant at every point of the Lobachevsky plane:

\[
\boxed{-1}
\]
